correctness.rationale: The weighted Matrix–Tree theorem gives objective det reduced Laplacian; strict logdet concavity holds in each individual edge because reduced Laplacian is injective on the full complete simple graph edge-weight vector, which proves unrestricted uniqueness. Permuting vertices within each community therefore forces class-constant weights a,b,c. The spectrum on within-community contrast modes and hub-group contrast yields T=c(pa+qc)^(p−1)(qb+pc)^(q−1). Homogeneity determines the Lagrange multiplier λ=(p+q−1)/B; direct KKT marginal returns r_a=2/(P(pa+qc)), r_b=2/(Q(qb+pc)), r_c=(1/c+q(p−1)/(pa+qc)+p(q−1)/(qb+pc))/(pq). Solving all four active sets with complementarity yields precisely the stated disjoint regions, including equality boundaries and c>0. At p=2,q=5,P=Q=6/5,B=1 independently computed a=0,b=7/234,c=5/78, expenditure 1 and returns r_a=26/5<λ=6, r_b=r_c=6. Infinite p,q and positive prices follow from analytic convex-program proof, not numeric tests.
